name: mMTC_CFSS
description: Generic configurable GST for massive Machine Type Communications (mMTC / MIoT) slices. Based on GSMA NG.116 v10.0. Providers can configure each attribute within the allowed ranges to describe their specific mMTC deployment.

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: Availability
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: (Communication service) availability: percentage value of the amount of time the end-to-end communication service is delivered according to an agreed QoS. For mMTC, moderate-to-high availability is typical; devices tolerate occasional disconnections.

value.alias: Standard mMTC availability - non-critical IoT sensors
High availability - smart metering, industrial IoT
Very high availability - smart grid, critical infrastructure

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: AreaOfService
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Area where UEs can access the mMTC network slice. mMTC deployments are typically national, regional (industrial zones, urban areas) or campus-level.

value.alias: Two-letter country code

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: AreaOfService.RegionSpecification
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Specifies whether the mMTC service covers a full country or specific regions (e.g. industrial park, urban district, campus).

value.alias: Full country coverage
Partial coverage - industrial zones, smart city districts, campus

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: DelayTolerance
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Core mMTC characteristic: devices tolerate service delivery delays (batch transmission, off-peak scheduling). Most mMTC use cases are delay-tolerant by nature. Not including this attribute equals Not supported.

value.alias: Delay tolerance not supported - real-time mMTC only
Delay tolerance supported - typical mMTC (sensors, metering)

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: UEDensity
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Maximum number of connected/accessible devices per km2. This is the defining KPI of mMTC. 3GPP TS 22.261 defines the mMTC target as up to 1,000,000 devices/km2.

value.alias: Industry 4.0 / Campus IoT
Massive IoT - smart city, smart metering (3GPP TS 22.261 target)

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: MaximumNumberOfUEs.MaximumNumberOfUEs
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Maximum number of UEs that can use the network slice simultaneously. For mMTC this can reach hundreds of millions of devices across the deployment area.

value.alias: Campus / industrial IoT deployment
National-scale mMTC - smart metering, smart city

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: MaximumNumberOfUEs.EPSCountingRequired
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Specifies if EPS (4G) UE counting must be included. Relevant when mMTC slice supports NB-IoT devices that may connect via LTE/EPS.

value.alias: EPS UE counting not required
EPS UE counting required - NB-IoT/eMTC via 4G

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: MaximumNumberOfUEs.RoamingUEsCountingRequired
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Specifies if roaming UEs are included in the device count. Relevant for cross-border IoT asset tracking use cases.

value.alias: Roaming UEs not counted
Roaming UEs counted - cross-border asset tracking

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: MaximumNumberOfPDUSessions.MaximumNumberOfPDUSessions
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Maximum concurrent PDU sessions. In mMTC, many devices are dormant and only a fraction have active sessions simultaneously (typical activation rate 1-10%).

value.alias: Typical mMTC concurrent sessions (1-10% activation rate)

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: MaximumNumberOfPDUSessions.EPSCountingRequired
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Whether EPS PDN connections are included in PDU session count. Relevant for NB-IoT/eMTC devices connecting via EPS.

value.alias: EPS counting not required
EPS counting required

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: MaximumNumberOfPDUSessions.LBOPDUSessionsCountingRequired
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Whether Local Breakout PDU sessions are counted.

value.alias: LBO sessions not counted
LBO sessions counted

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: NBIoTSupport
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Specifies if NB-IoT (Narrowband IoT) is supported in the RAN. NB-IoT is a key 3GPP radio access technology for mMTC, providing extended coverage, low power consumption and support for massive device density. Applies to 3GPP access type only.

value.alias: NB-IoT not supported - eMTC or NR RedCap only
NB-IoT supported - massive IoT, smart metering, agriculture

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: EnergyEfficiency
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Describes whether the slice supports energy efficiency KPI monitoring. Critical for mMTC where battery-powered devices must operate for years without recharge (3GPP TS 22.261 target: 10+ years battery life).

value.alias: Energy efficiency KPI not monitored
Energy efficiency KPI supported - battery life monitoring

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: MaximumSupportedPacketSize
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Maximum packet size supported. mMTC devices typically send very small payloads (sensor readings, telemetry). Packet size directly impacts NB-IoT/eMTC transport efficiency.

value.alias: IoT small packet - sensor telemetry, NB-IoT payload
Standard MTU - firmware OTA update, image upload

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: DeterministicCommunication.Availability
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Defines if the slice supports deterministic communication for periodic mMTC traffic. Key for smart metering (fixed reporting intervals), industrial sensors, and precision agriculture. Applies to 3GPP access only.

value.alias: Aperiodic/event-driven mMTC traffic only
Periodic traffic supported - metering, environmental monitoring

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: DeterministicCommunication.Periodicity
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: List of periodicities supported for mMTC periodic traffic. mMTC reporting intervals range from seconds (industrial sensors) to hours (utility metering). Must be present when DeterministicCommunication.Availability is Supported.

value.alias: 1s–60s - industrial sensor, environmental monitoring
1min–1h - smart metering, agriculture telemetry
1h–24h - daily utility meter read

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: Synchronicity.Availability
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Synchronicity between BS and UE, or between UEs. Relevant for coordinated mMTC transmissions (synchronized sensor networks, smart grid PMU). Applies to 3GPP access only.

value.alias: No synchronicity - asynchronous IoT devices
BS-to-UE sync - synchronized metering, smart grid PMU

value.value: Between BS and UE & UE and UE
value.alias: Full sync - coordinated sensor networks

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: Synchronicity.Accuracy
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Accuracy of synchronicity. For mMTC, typical accuracy ranges from 1 microsecond (precision grid) to 1 millisecond (standard IoT coordination). Must be present when Synchronicity.Availability is not 'Not supported'.

value.alias: 1µs–1ms - smart grid PMU to sensor coordination

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: SupportForNonIPTraffic
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Non-IP session support (Ethernet, unstructured data). Many mMTC devices use non-IP protocols (CoAP over UDP, MQTT, proprietary sensor protocols) or require Ethernet PDU sessions for industrial IoT. Not including this equals Not supported.

value.alias: IP only - standard IP-based IoT protocols
Non-IP Ethernet sessions supported - industrial IoT, Modbus, proprietary sensors

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: SliceQualityOfService.5QI
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: 5QI scalar referencing 5G QoS characteristics. For mMTC, relevant standardised 5QIs per 3GPP TS 23.501 Table 5.7.4-1 are 5QI=6 (Non-GBR, PDB=300ms, IoT) and 5QI=9 (default Non-GBR). Providers may also use operator-specific 5QI values.

value.value: Standardised 5QI values per Table 5.7.4-1 of 3GPP TS 23.501 or Operator-specific 5QI values per Table 9.11.4.12.1 of 3GPP TS 24.501
value.alias: mMTC typical: 5QI=6 (300ms PDB) or 5QI=9 (default Non-GBR)

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: SliceQualityOfService.ResourceType
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Resource type for mMTC QoS flows. mMTC is predominantly Non-GBR (best effort, no guaranteed rate). GBR may apply to critical mMTC (e.g. smart grid control).

value.alias: Non-Guaranteed Bit Rate - typical mMTC sensors, metering
Guaranteed Bit Rate - critical mMTC (smart grid control)

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: SliceQualityOfService.PriorityLevel
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Priority in scheduling resources. mMTC is typically low priority (high number = low priority). Range 1 (highest) to 127 (lowest) per 3GPP TS 23.501.

value.alias: High priority mMTC - critical infrastructure, smart grid
Low priority mMTC - standard sensors, metering, agriculture

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: SliceQualityOfService.PacketDelayBudget
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Upper bound for packet delay between UE and UPF. mMTC is delay-tolerant: typical PDB ranges from 300ms (standard IoT) to 10s (batch/delay-tolerant). Per 3GPP TS 23.501.

value.alias: 300ms–10s - typical mMTC PDB range (3GPP TS 23.501 5QI=6: 300ms)

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: SliceQualityOfService.PacketErrorRate
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Upper bound for PDU error rate. mMTC typically accepts higher PER than URLLC. Per 3GPP TS 23.501, standard Non-GBR IoT PER is 10^-6 to 10^-4.

value.alias: 10^-6 to 10^-4 - standard mMTC PER per 3GPP TS 23.501

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: SliceQualityOfService.GuaranteedFlowBitRateDownlink
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: GFBR Downlink per GBR QoS flow. For mMTC GBR flows (critical IoT), typical values are very low (1–100 kbps per device for control/actuation).

value.alias: 0 = Non-GBR (default); up to 100 kbps for critical mMTC GBR flows

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: SliceQualityOfService.GuaranteedFlowBitRateUplink
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: GFBR Uplink per GBR QoS flow. mMTC uplink is dominant (sensor data upload). GBR applies to critical sensors only.

value.alias: 0 = Non-GBR (default); up to 100 kbps for critical uplink sensors

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: SliceQualityOfService.MaximumFlowBitRateDownlink
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: MFBR Downlink per QoS flow. For mMTC DL (actuation/configuration), typical max is 1–250 kbps per NB-IoT/eMTC device.

value.alias: 1–1000 kbps - NB-IoT: ~250 kbps DL max, eMTC: ~1 Mbps DL max

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: SliceQualityOfService.MaximumFlowBitRateUplink
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: MFBR Uplink per QoS flow. mMTC UL (sensor data) is the primary traffic direction. NB-IoT max UL ~250 kbps, eMTC ~1 Mbps.

value.alias: 1–1000 kbps - NB-IoT: ~250 kbps UL max, eMTC: ~1 Mbps UL max

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: SliceQualityOfService.MaximumPacketLossRate
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Maximum tolerable packet loss rate for mMTC QoS flows. mMTC typically accepts higher loss than URLLC, relying on application-layer retransmission.

value.alias: 0 to 10^-3 - mMTC acceptable loss (retransmission at app layer)

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: DownlinkThroughputPerNetworkSlice.GuaranteedDownlinkThroughputQuota
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Guaranteed aggregate DL throughput for the slice. mMTC DL is typically low (devices receive small config/actuation payloads). 0 = best effort.

value.alias: 0 (best effort) to 1 Gbps aggregate for massive device DL

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: DownlinkThroughputPerNetworkSlice.MaximumDownlinkThroughput
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Maximum aggregate DL throughput for all mMTC devices combined. Sized by device count × per-device DL rate.

value.alias: 1 Mbps to 10 Gbps aggregate DL - scales with device population

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: UplinkThroughputPerNetworkSlice.GuaranteedUplinkThroughputQuota
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Guaranteed aggregate UL throughput. UL is the dominant direction in mMTC (sensor data upload). 0 = best effort.

value.alias: 0 (best effort) to 1 Gbps aggregate UL for massive device reporting

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: UplinkThroughputPerNetworkSlice.MaximumUplinkThroughput
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Maximum aggregate UL throughput for all mMTC devices. UL is primary traffic in mMTC.

value.alias: 1 Mbps to 10 Gbps aggregate UL - scales with device population and reporting rate

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: DownlinkMaximumThroughputPerUE.MaximumDownlinkThroughputPerUEValue
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Maximum DL data rate per individual mMTC device. NB-IoT peak DL: ~250 kbps. eMTC peak DL: ~1 Mbps. Standard sensor devices: 1–10 kbps.

value.alias: 1–250 kbps - NB-IoT range (sensor config, firmware delta OTA)
250 kbps–1 Mbps - eMTC range (larger OTA, image upload)

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: DownlinkMaximumThroughputPerUE.ServiceCategory
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Optional service category label for per-UE DL throughput differentiation within the mMTC slice.

value.value: Any text identifying the Service Category
value.alias: Service category label

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: UplinkMaximumThroughputPerUE.MaximumUplinkThroughputPerUEValue
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Maximum UL data rate per mMTC device. This is the primary KPI for sensor data upload. NB-IoT peak UL: ~250 kbps. eMTC peak UL: ~1 Mbps. Typical mMTC sensor: 1–10 kbps.

value.alias: 1–250 kbps - NB-IoT range (typical sensor telemetry: 1–10 kbps)
250 kbps–1 Mbps - eMTC range (video surveillance IoT, asset tracking)

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: UplinkMaximumThroughputPerUE.ServiceCategory
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Optional service category label for per-UE UL throughput differentiation.

value.value: Any text identifying the Service Category
value.alias: Service category label

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: SessionAndServiceContinuitySupport
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: PDU session continuity mode. mMTC devices may be mobile (asset tracking) or stationary. SSC mode 1 (IP preserved) suits stationary devices; SSC mode 2/3 suits mobile IoT that tolerates reconnection.

value.alias: IP address preserved - stationary sensors, smart meters
PDU session may be released - mobile IoT, asset tracking
New anchor before old released - mobility-tolerant IoT

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: SupportedDeviceVelocity
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Maximum UE speed at which QoS and handover are maintained. mMTC covers stationary (smart meters, fixed sensors) to mobile (vehicle tracking, logistics). High-speed vehicular not typical for mMTC.

value.alias: Stationary - smart meters, fixed environmental sensors
Pedestrian - wearable IoT, healthcare monitoring
Vehicular - logistics tracking, fleet management, connected vehicles

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: RadioSpectrum
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Radio spectrum bands for the mMTC slice. NB-IoT and eMTC operate in sub-GHz and low-band spectrum for extended coverage and building penetration (key mMTC requirement). Applies to 3GPP access type only.

value.value: NR operating band identifiers per 3GPP TS 38.101-1
value.alias: mMTC relevant: n1(2100MHz), n3(1800MHz), n8(900MHz), n28(700MHz) for coverage; n77/n78 for dense industrial

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: PerformanceMonitoring.Availability
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: KQI/KPI monitoring capabilities available for the mMTC slice. Providers select which metrics to monitor.

value.alias: SRSR monitoring - device attach/detach success rate

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: PerformanceMonitoring.MonitoringSampleFrequency
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Frequency at which KQIs/KPIs are sampled. mMTC monitoring can be less frequent than eMBB given delay-tolerant nature.

value.alias: 1Hz - real-time monitoring for critical mMTC
Per minute - standard mMTC monitoring
Per hour - lightweight monitoring for large-scale mMTC deployments

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: MonitoringAndAnalytics
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Root cause analysis and proactive monitoring capability. Useful for managing massive device fleets in mMTC deployments.

value.alias: No analytics
NSC informed about root causes - fleet anomaly reporting
NSC can investigate proactively - predictive maintenance IoT

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: SupportedDataNetwork.SupportedDataNetworkList
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Data networks accessible by the mMTC slice (e.g. IoT platform DNN, private industrial network, Internet).

value.value: Text identification of one data network or a list of data networks
value.alias: e.g. IoT-Platform DNN, Industrial-LAN, Internet

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: SupportedDataNetwork.ServiceCategory
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Service category associated with a supported data network in the mMTC slice.

value.value: Any text identifying the service category
value.alias: Service category label

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: DataNetworkAccess.DataAccessPerDataNetwork
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: How the mMTC slice handles user data for each data network. Industrial IoT typically uses private network termination; consumer IoT uses direct internet access.

value.alias: Internet breakout - consumer IoT, cloud-connected sensors
VPN/tunnel to private network - industrial IoT, smart grid, enterprise
Fully local - campus IoT, closed factory network

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: DataNetworkAccess.TunnellingMechanism
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Tunnelling mechanism for private network connectivity. Relevant for industrial mMTC connecting to on-premise IoT platforms.

value.alias: Layer 2 Tunnelling Protocol
Generic Routing Encapsulation
Virtual Private Network - typical for industrial IoT
MPLS-style label routing
Operator-defined tunnelling

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: DataNetworkAccess.LBOAllowed
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Whether Local Breakout is allowed while roaming. Relevant for cross-border asset tracking mMTC use cases.

value.alias: LBO allowed - cross-border IoT asset tracking
LBO not allowed - domestic deployments only

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: NSSAARequired
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Network Slice-Specific Authentication and Authorization. For mMTC, slice-level AAA is recommended when serving multiple enterprise tenants or sensitive IoT verticals (smart grid, healthcare).

value.alias: No slice-specific AAA - basic IoT deployment
Slice-specific AAA - enterprise IoT, smart grid, healthcare

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: SimultaneousUseOfNetworkSlice.SimultaneousUseClass
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Defines whether the mMTC slice can be used simultaneously with other slices. mMTC devices typically use a dedicated slice and may not need simultaneous use.

value.value: Can be used simultaneously with any network slice
value.alias: No simultaneous use restriction

value.value: Can be used simultaneously with any network slices with same SST value but different SD values
value.alias: Same SST only

value.value: Cannot be used simultaneously with any another network slice
value.alias: Exclusive use - dedicated mMTC tenant
Operator-specific rule

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: NetworkFunctionsOwnedByNSC
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: List of network functions that the NSC (tenant/enterprise) owns and provides for this mMTC slice. Common in private IoT networks.

value.alias: e.g. UDM, AUSF, AF, IoT-NEF

serviceSpecCharacteristic.name: UserManagementOpenness
serviceSpecCharacteristic.description: Capability for the NSC to manage device (UE) subscriptions and groups. Critical for enterprise mMTC deployments managing large device fleets.

value.alias: NSC cannot manage devices
NSC can add/modify/delete device subscriptions - fleet management
